criteria.no: At least one term that decides compliance is a subjective quality, an undefined label, tier, or mode, an unidentified expected output or standard, or an approval with no identified record.
criteria.unclear: A term may not be understood, but it cannot be told whether it decides compliance.
criteria.yes: Every term that decides compliance is understood.

self_contained.instructions: Look at each term in `anchor.statement` that decides compliance, one at a time. A term is understood when it is a command, subcommand, flag, file or directory path, commit hash, error or diagnostic code, report or record id, value, environment variable, format, stream, a role such as 'the caller', or a term the statement defines inline; a statement may name many such records and still be fully understood. A term is not understood when it is a subjective quality (robust, clean), a label, tier, or mode the statement never defines (R7, Mode K), an expected output or standard whose record the statement does not identify, or a person's approval with no identified record. Sentence form, who is told to act, bundled duties, and details beyond the quote do not matter here.

anchor.statement: The lint report written to out/lint.json must list each of the diagnostics W001-unused-import, W014-shadowed-name, and E203-missing-return by its code.
anchor.quote: out/lint.json has to list W001-unused-import, W014-shadowed-name and E203-missing-return by their codes
